chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Ayoub, brother of Adeym, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, 'From where should the children undress (and wear Ihram)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to get them to undress (and wear Ihram) from Fakkhan'.
ai.seo_question: Where should children enter Ihram for Hajj according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific location known as 'Fakk' (or Fakkhan) from which young children are released from their state of Ihram, highlighting the practical application of the ruling that children are not bound by the same restrictions as adults. It reflects the scholarly tradition of tracing jurisprudential details back to the Imams, with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) citing the practice of his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), to establish a precedent for the age of religious accountability in Hajj rituals.
